fields.meta_description: Emergent builds order processing automation that reads each emailed PO, checks credit and stock, and syncs clean orders to your ERP.
fields.h1: Build Order Processing Automation That Checks Every Line
fields.hero_description: Build order processing automation that turns emailed POs into checked sales orders and holds only what needs a person.
fields.features_subheading: Order management automation reads each new order and runs your team's checks, leaving people only the lines that need a decision.
fields.feature_1:
Orders read from email and PDF

Customer POs sent as PDF attachments or typed into an email become a draft sales order with the customer, lines, quantities, prices, and ship-to. Unclear fields go to a person.
fields.feature_2:
Lines checked against your price list

Each line is matched to your catalog by part number and priced from the customer's contract. A quoted price that disagrees, or an unknown part number, holds that line for its rep.
fields.feature_3:
Credit checked before release

The open balance plus the new order is checked against the customer's credit limit before release. An order over the limit waits while the credit manager gets a direct message.
fields.feature_4:
Stock reserved when an order is released

Released lines reserve stock on hand. A short line ships what is there and backorders the rest, and the warehouse works from one pick list built from the day's released orders.
fields.feature_5:
One orders table, synced to your ERP

Email, store, and phone orders land in one table with one status each. Released orders sync to NetSuite or QuickBooks, and buyers look up their own progress by PO number.
fields.feature_6:
Order rules you can read and export

Every hold rule and price check is readable code you can export to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Orders, holds, and backorders sit in a database that your team owns.

fields.tab_content_1:
PO 7731 arrives as a PDF and leaves as SO-50388

Harlow Hardware emails its orders to Calder Supply as PDFs. The app reads PO 7731 into sales order SO-50388, four lines in all. Three match the contract. Drawer slides come in at $12.75 against a contract price of $14.20, and any price that differs from the contract holds its line for Maren Liu, the account rep.
fields.tab_content_2:
An $8,400 order waits on the credit manager

Pinecrest Supply owes $18,900 on open invoices against a $25,000 credit limit. Its new $8,400 order would take the balance to $27,300. Any order that takes an account over its limit is held before the warehouse sees it. Odile Varga in credit is messaged in Slack and releases it there or asks Pinecrest for prepayment.
fields.tab_content_3:
Short on towels, the order ships in two parts

Every line is checked against stock before release to the warehouse. SO-50412 asks for 120 cases of shop towels, and 90 are on hand. Those 90 go on today's pick list with the rest of the order, and the other 30 go on backorder against the next receipt. The buyer gets one email that lists both shipments.
fields.tab_content_4:
Buyers find any order by their own PO number

Buyers at Brindle Cafe Group used to email customer service to ask where an order stood. Ana Reyes now types PO 2290 into Calder Supply's status page and sees SO-50441 packed and waiting on a label. The carrier and tracking number fill in once the label is bought, read from the same table the warehouse updates.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up order processing automation that checks every incoming order, tested on a week of real orders first.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Load price lists and credit limits
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every way orders reach you today: the orders inbox, PDF attachments, your web store, EDI from large accounts, and calls the desk types up. Note which ones carry a customer PO number, since that number ties each order, hold, and shipment together.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write your hold rules as plain sentences: a quoted price off the contract, a new order that pushes an account past its credit limit, a part number missing from the catalog. Name the person who decides each one. A hold without an owner sits forever.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Import each customer's contract prices and credit limit, with open balances from your accounting system. Emergent builds the checks against those tables. An account manager can then change a price later without anyone touching the rules themselves.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the system that holds your orders and stock, such as NetSuite or QuickBooks. Stock levels sync in before each release and released orders sync back with their status. For order fulfillment automation, the pick list reads from that same table.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set a backorder policy per account
fields.howto_step_5_des: Some accounts accept partial shipments. Others want the whole order held until every line is in stock. Store that choice on each customer record, and the release step follows it without a phone call to ask which one the buyer prefers.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Replay a week of real orders
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run seven days of past orders through the app before launch and compare each hold with what the desk did by hand. Where the app held something your team released, adjust the rule by prompting and run the batch again until both agree.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Start with your largest PDF senders
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn on automated order management for the five customers who send the most PDF orders. Have the desk review each draft for the first two weeks. Once the holds look right, let clean orders release on their own and add the next accounts.
